The *Piyālaphaladāyakattheraapadāna* is a canonical verse text preserved in the *Therāpadāna* of the Pali Khuddaka Nikāya [SuttaCentral]. As suggested by its title, the poem recounts the past merit of a thera who offered a *piyāla* fruit (Buchanania cochinchinensis) and experienced the karmic fruits of that gift across lifetimes. SuttaCentral records five modern translations across five languages for this entry [SuttaCentral].

No external parallels in Sanskrit, Chinese, or Tibetan are identified by SuttaCentral or detected with significant similarity by DharmaNexus [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. Within the Pali tradition, the text exhibits extensive formulaic text reuse: DharmaNexus registers 161 matching segments across 68 Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. Its closest intertextual connection is with the *Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā* (first part), with which it shares 19 matching passages (including segments §0.3–4.1) [DharmaNexus]. In addition, it shares standardized biographical and merit-proclaiming verses with numerous other Apadāna poems describing fruit offerings, such as the *Kāsumāriphaladāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 382), the *Mātuluṅgaphaladāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 508), the *Kurañciyaphaladāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 513), and the *Labujaphaladāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 469) [DharmaNexus].
